slides.texte_overlay:
how to become unbelievably
articulate nd wellspoken

slow down by a third

speak a third slower than feels natural for one week. slower speech sounds more confident, gives you time to think, and makes people actually stop and listen.

kill the filler words

notice every um, like and you know, and replace them with a short pause. a silence sounds thoughtful, a filler word sounds unsure, and people hear the difference.

read aloud every night

read two pages of a good book out loud before bed. it trains your mouth to handle long sentences and fills your memory with better words without effort.

have more to say

spend 5 minutes a day learning one new idea: a word's origin, a moment in history, a scientific concept. articulate people aren't just clear, they have more to talk about.
slides.texte_sophia:
have more to say

i used to run out of things to say. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: a word's origin, a moment in history. articulate people simply have more to say.

slides.texte_overlay:
end with a point

finish every answer with one clear sentence that sums up what you meant. people remember the last thing you say, so make it the clearest and sharpest part of all.
